evidence.SUPPORTED: passed its pre-registered test in both periods after costs on its tier
evidence.WEAK: passed thinly (few events, one tier, near the bar)
evidence.CONFLICTING: helped in one period or tier and hurt in another

permission.PAPER: may be a reason in a paper decision (inside its tier)
permission.CONTEXT: shown and explained, never a reason to trade
permission.LIVE_PROVEN: enough live paper evidence to be considered for real money (none yet)

meaning.unavailable: a runtime flag: its data is missing or stale right now, which always means no trade

rule: Jarvis acts only on PAPER (or LIVE_PROVEN) cards and says the evidence word whenever it uses an idea. A CONTEXT or OFF idea may be described, never given as a reason to buy.

cards.name: Bitcoin 50-day rule (market gate)
cards.reason: Inside zones 68% held when the market was allowed vs 50% when not; the trend book's crash insurance

cards.name: Trend book T3 on the 10 coins
cards.reason: Passed both periods after costs on the liquid top-30 tier (#15); on all 120 coins it did not beat random, it only cut losses. The earlier 10-coin pass (#4) is the basic-lab era, rated legacy in the Oct 14 audit: never cite it as evidence. Point-in-time check on the 10 (#30): passes both periods but much weaker, +3.7% in 2024-26 (today's 10: +15.1%; holding lost 31.9%).

cards.name: T3-B sizing (re-size only when far off)
cards.reason: Same or better with a third of the trades on today's 10 and 30 (#20). On the coins as they really were each month: fails its profit rule on the 30 (#22: -22.5% in 2024-26 while holding lost 76%); passes on the 10 but much weaker (#30: +3.7% in 2024-26 vs +15.1% on today's 10; holding the same coins lost 31.9%). Do not quote +15.1% as its edge.

cards.name: Trend book on the 30-coin tier
cards.reason: Evidence only, never a candidate for real money (Madhav, Oct 15). Passed on today's top 30 (#15) but failed the survivorship check (#22): -22.5% vs holding -76% in 2024-26

cards.name: Short dip trade (H07)
cards.reason: One measured cell: tier-A coins while the exposure dial is CLOSED, +5.1% a trade over random after costs in both periods (review #26), confirmed point-in-time on all 530 Binance pairs with dead coins and live costs, +6.3% a trade expected (review #29); no stop, 10-day exit (#27). On the broad 120, in other tiers, or with the dial open: no measured edge. Its live book's 8-for-8 was one signal day (Oct 8), dial open, outside the measured cell: 1 independent event.

cards.reason: Fell under the bar on 120 coins (#16): watched only

cards.name: The lookout inside a zone (wick, close back above, volume, divergence)
cards.reason: Added nothing beyond arithmetic (#7)

cards.name: Hold past the next zone (no zone targets)
cards.reason: A lesson kept from a failed test. Review #10 tested a stop under the zone with a sell target at the next zone and it FAILED: the next zone is near, so the target sold the few big moves early. Holding instead did better in both periods (target 0.0% a trade vs +5.8% for holding 20 days in 2018-23, z 3.4; -1.3% vs +0.3% in 2024-26), on the 10 coins only, never re-tested on more. Kept: no zone targets; the next zone is a review point, not a sell.

cards.name: Looser trailing exits
cards.reason: Won in 2018-23, lost in 2024-26; the 20-day exit survived both (#12)

cards.name: Structural stops (1 daily range under the structure)
cards.reason: Beat tight percent stops; the dip trade is best with no stop (#18)

cards.name: Zone-trade stop (close half a range under the zone)
cards.reason: Never passed a test of its own. Review #10 tested this stop together with a sell target at the next zone and that FAILED (the target cut the winners). A look decided after that run (exploratory, not a test) found the stop without a target, held up to 60 days, did about as well as just holding (+18.1% vs +20.8% in 2018-23, +3.2% vs +4.5% since 2024): it rarely saved much. Kept by design as the point where a zone trade's idea is wrong (the decision chain), not as a measured edge.
